newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere head under investigation over complaints.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere head under investigation over complaints.

text.p: Jean-Luc Lagardere, chairman of the Lagardere group, said in a newspaper interview on Saturday he was placed under legal investigation on October 28 in connection with complaints filed by shareholders when his Matra missile unit merged with book publisher Hachette in 1992.
The complaints focused mainly on the control exercised over Matra-Hachette by the Lagardere group, a partnership with limited shares, and on a system of fees paid to its managers.
In the interview with the French daily Le Figaro, Lagardere also defended a controversial government plan to sell state-owned defence and electronics group Thomson SA to the Lagardere group.

France announced in mid-October that it favoured a takeover proposal from Lagardere for Thomson SA. It plans to recapitalise Thomson with 11 billion francs before selling it to Lagardere for a symbolic one franc.
Lagardere in turn plans to sell Thomson Multimedia (TMM), the consumer electronics branch of Thomson SA, to South Korean group Daewoo Electronics Co for one franc.
Lagardere will retain the Thomson-CSF defence branch and merge it with its own Matra unit.
Criticism of the plan has mostly focused on Daewoo Electronics acquiring the leading-edge digital television technology of Thomson Multimedia too cheaply.
Lagardere, seeking to counter criticism over the sale, said Daewoo and Lagardere planned to invest a total of over 26 billion francs in Thomson SA.
Daewoo has already pledged to spend at least 10 billion francs on TMM.
Lagardere also confirmed that Daewoo had pledged to maintain jobs at TMM and create a further 5,000 jobs in France.
